irac.issue: Whether Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended in 2005, confers a right on a daughter to claim a share in the property on an equal footing with her brother, and whether the said right is available only to daughters born after the amendment or to all daughters irrespective of their birth.
irac.rule: Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended in 2005, confers a right on a daughter to claim a share in the property on an equal footing with her brother. The said right is available to all daughters irrespective of their birth.
irac.application: The Court applied the amended Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, to the facts of the case and held that the daughter has a right to claim a share in the property on an equal footing with her brother, irrespective of her birth.
irac.conclusion: The Court upheld the amendment to Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, and held that a daughter has a right to claim a share in the property on an equal footing with her brother, irrespective of her birth.
